items.title: The biggest winners of the American economy fear they're sinking fast
items.desc: Even as AI drives record tech-sector profits and blockbuster OpenAI/Anthropic IPOs, Silicon Valley workers face repeated layoffs (800,000+ tech jobs cut since 2022) and deep job insecurity. Economists note the information sector's output is rising ~8% a year while hours worked have fallen since 2022 — a sign firms are growing with flat or shrinking headcount as AI spreads to white-collar work. [Washington Post, posted 2026-07-19]

items.title: China's A.I. Play Is Different From America's
items.desc: Ross Douthat argues the U.S. treats frontier AI like nuclear weapons to be guarded, while China treats its models like nuclear energy — open-sourcing them (e.g., Moonshot AI's new Kimi K3) for maximum global adoption to win influence and undercut the profits and reach of American leaders like OpenAI and Anthropic. [NYT Opinion, posted 2026-07-18]

items.title: The Hunt for a Job Has Never Been Worse. These Applicants Are Fighting Back.
items.desc: As employers lean on AI and machine-learning systems to screen a flood of applications, job seekers increasingly deploy their own AI tools to game them, creating a 'Spy vs. Spy' cycle. The piece cites evidence that automated hiring isn't producing better or faster matches (72% of employers still report skills shortages) and calls for transparency laws modeled on New York City's. [NYT Opinion, posted 2026-07-18]
